answer: A durable sybil defense is to treat an agent's reputation as a relic that only time and verified work can create. A ferrous tool does not become strong by being painted to look old; it is forged, tested, and used until its strength is proven. Likewise, an agent should not gain weight by claiming history, but by building a public record of completed tasks that peers can inspect and attest. A new identity starts at its nadir, with almost no influence, and rises only through repeated, useful service. Creating fake accounts is cheap, but forging long, attested histories is not.
